name: Coloboma of choroid and retina
aliases: Ocular coloboma involving choroid and retina

criteria.description: Presence of a well-demarcated, excavated defect in the choroid and retina visible on fundoscopic examination
Visual field defects corresponding to the location of the coloboma
Confirmation of chorioretinal defect by ocular imaging modalities such as OCT or fundus photography
Exclusion of other ocular malformations or syndromic features that could explain the findings

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic chorioretinal defect on fundoscopic examination confirmed by ocular imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be considered if syndromic association is suspected.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chorioretinal excavation visible on fundus examination
searchTerms: retinal excavation visible in eye exam

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visual field defect corresponding to coloboma location
searchTerms: visual field missing where coloboma is
blind spot corresponding to eye defect

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced visual acuity related to coloboma extent
searchTerms: reduced sharpness of vision from coloboma
poor eyesight related to eye defect size
decreased visual clarity due to coloboma
optic nerve coloboma causing vision issues

imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating retinal and choroidal excavation
Fluorescein angiography may show abnormal vasculature
other: Visual field testing demonstrating corresponding defects
Electroretinography may show localized retinal dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: Coloboma primarily involves optic nerve head rather than choroid and retina
Retinal detachment presents acutely with visual loss and no congenital excavation
Distinct funnel-shaped excavation of optic disc

redFlags: Sudden onset of visual loss indicating possible retinal detachment
Signs of increased intraocular pressure suggesting glaucoma
references: Chang B, et al. Coloboma of the eye: clinical features and molecular genetics. Eye (Lond). 2020.
Orphanet: Coloboma of choroid and retina. ORPHA:98942.
American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern: Congenital Anomalies of the Eye. 2019.
